title: Doorway
premise:
Three in the morning behind a restaurant that closed at one. A service corridor: brick on one side, the blank back wall of the neighbouring building on the other, a single sodium lamp, bins, and a steel service door with a mechanical lock. A courier has a package that has to be inside that door before the morning delivery, and no key. The building's night porter is already in the corridor, sitting on an upturned crate, because that is where they always sit.

Write it close and quiet. Present tense. No violence — the pressure is that both of these people have good reasons and neither can simply leave.

scenes.question: Does Riven get through the door before Merritt decides what to do about them?

writerStyle:
Close third on the POV character, present tense. Concrete nouns. Let the corridor do the work — sound,
cold, the smell off the bins — rather than adjectives about mood.

Dialogue is sparse and does not explain itself. People talk past each other, answer a question with
a different question, and leave sentences unfinished when the other person already knows the end.

No omniscience: if the POV character cannot see, hear or reasonably infer it, it does not go on the
page. Never state what a non-POV character is feeling — show what they do and let it stand.

Paragraphs short. Prefer the plain word. Cut any sentence whose only job is to tell the reader how
to feel about the previous one.

characters.name: RIVEN
characters.persona:
Riven

Late twenties. Courier for four years, the last two on the night runs nobody else wants, because the
night runs pay for the room and the room is not negotiable. Carries a flat parcel in a canvas
satchel, taped, unmarked, about the size of a hardback book.

Riven is not a thief and would be genuinely offended to be called one — but has picked a lock before,
twice, both times for a client who had locked themselves out, and both times it took longer than
expected and left them sweating. They are competent, not slick.
characters.knows: The package must be inside before the 5am delivery or the contract is gone. There is supposed to be nobody in this corridor at this hour.
characters.goal: Get the package through that door and be gone before 5am — whatever it takes to get past whoever's in the way tonight.
characters.belief: Whoever is sitting in this corridor is not supposed to be here either — a mistake, and mistakes can be talked around.
characters.impulse: When cornered, get politer, not louder — explain yourself, even knowing the explaining usually makes it worse.
voice: "I'm early. Delivery's at five. You didn't see me being early."
skills: lockpicking :: opening a mechanical lock without its key, given time and quiet
climbing :: getting up and over a wall or a stack of crates

characters.name: MERRITT
characters.persona:
Merritt

Sixty-one. Night porter at Kessel's for nine years, blind for six of them — a slow retinal thing
that finished the job it started. Kept the post because the building is a building they already knew
by heart, and because the manager could not find the sentence that would end it.

Sits on the same upturned crate every night between two and four, out in the corridor rather than in
the office, because the corridor is where you hear the whole block: the compressor, the gate, the
gulls on the flat roof, anyone coming.
characters.knows: The service door lock has been sticking for a month and nobody has fixed it. Head office has asked twice this year why the night log is so short.
characters.goal: Get through this shift without a single thing happening that they can't account for in the log — another unexplained gap is what finally costs them this job.
characters.belief: A night where nothing happens cannot be held against you — keep the corridor quiet and the ledger has nothing to say.
characters.impulse: When handled as though the blindness were the interesting fact in the room, go hard and stop giving room — without raising your voice.
voice: "You're standing two feet nearer the door than when you started."
"Which key did you say you had?"
skills: keys :: knowing by feel which key on the ring opens which door in this building
